sections.h2: Who sends the Pierce County tax bill
sections.html:
Pierce County combines valuing and collecting in a single Assessor-Treasurer's Office, so your assessment notice and your payment both go through the same door. Go to 2401 South 35th Street, Room 142, Tacoma, weekdays between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. To hand over a payment, Pierce County Finance, 1501 Market St., Suite 120, is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

  • Assessment and tax questions: (253) 798-6111.
  • Automated payment and balance line: (253) 798-3333. Have your parcel number ready.
  • Mail a check made out to Pierce County to Pierce County Finance, P.O. Box 11621, Tacoma, WA 98411-6621, enclosing the remittance stub or writing the parcel number on it.
  • An outside vendor processes card and e-check payments and charges extra: 2.35% on credit cards, $0.50 per e-check and $3.50 per debit card.

sections.h2: Pierce County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Tacoma anchors the county, which had about 946,288 residents in July 2025, behind only King County. Puyallup, Lakewood, University Place, Gig Harbor, Bonney Lake and Sumner are among the cities, and parts of Auburn, Enumclaw, Milton and Pacific reach in as well. One county office bills a house in any of them.

Homeownership sits at 64.7%, across 382,172 housing units. Median value of an owner-occupied home is $526,600 and median household income is $99,564. About a quarter of workers commute to King County, which keeps demand tied to the wider Puget Sound market.

Pay half by April 30 and half by October 31. The county shifts a weekend deadline to the following Monday, which happened with October 31 in 2026. Anyone still owing the second half should phone the office for an exact balance that includes interest.

Splitting the bill is a right only when it totals $50 or more. Under RCW 84.56.020, interest on late tax is worked out monthly. Homes with one to four units pay 0.75% a month (9% a year) on the whole year's tax from May 1, with penalties barred. Bigger apartment buildings and personal property pay 1% a month and penalties on top.

DateWhat happens
April 30First half is due.
May 1Interest starts on the full-year tax if the first half is unpaid: 0.75% per month on homes of one to four units for tax year 2023 and later, 1% per month on other property.
June 1Three percent penalty on other property.
October 31 (moves to Monday if a weekend)Second half is due.
December 1Additional eight percent penalty on other property, for an 11% total.

If no statement reaches you by March 31 and a mortgage company does not pay your taxes, call (253) 798-6111 for a copy.

sections.h2: How the county values your house
sections.html:
Every year the Assessor-Treasurer values each property at 100% of true and fair market value, the price a willing buyer would pay a willing seller. Assessed values track the market in both directions. Neighborhood desirability, building costs and improvements you have made all feed into the number.

A revaluation plan approved by the Washington Department of Revenue calls for a visit about every six years. Visits can happen sooner after new construction, a board case, an appraisal review, a sales verification or a split of the parcel. You may refuse private access, but not to the assessor or staff. To confirm a staff member's credentials, call (253) 798-6111.

Countywide, taxes total almost $2.1 billion, paying for schools, libraries, parks and emergency services.

sections.h2: How to appeal your Pierce County assessment
sections.html:
Appeals are filed with the Pierce County Board of Equalization. You can file up to July 1 of the assessment year, or up to 60 days after a value change notice was mailed, if that gives more time. For the form, call (253) 798-7415. RCW 84.40.038 also lets a board excuse a late filing for good cause.

You need specific reasons why the assessor's number differs from market value (RCW 84.40.0301). The size of the increase, personal hardship, the amount of the tax and anything unrelated to market value cannot be weighed. Reasons that count as good cause:

  • A death or serious illness affecting you or close family.
  • Incorrect written filing advice from board or assessor staff.
  • A flood, earthquake or similar disaster.
  • A mail delay the Postal Service has documented.

Missed July 1? A notice mailed in the last 60 days may still leave you time.

The county offers an exemption that lowers the tax and a deferral that postpones it. Eligibility for the exemption is widening. From January 2027, bills drop for more homeowners who are 61 or older or have a qualifying disability. The new tier requires:

  • You owned and lived in the home at least six months in 2026.
  • You turned 61 in 2026, or you are a veteran with at least a 40% disability rating, or a taxpayer with a qualifying disability who did not serve.
  • Combined household income is $85,000 or less for 2026, with a standard deduction for items such as medical premiums and prescription drugs.

Owners who met the earlier rules in 2023, 2024 or 2025 can still apply and could receive a refund. For those years the limit was income up to $64,000 and a veteran rating of at least 80%.

The deferral is a different animal. Reapply each year. You need to be 60 or older on December 31 of the year you apply, with yearly income under $68,319. The state's Department of Revenue pays the county on your behalf, and what it pays becomes a lien that you repay with interest when the home changes hands (RCW 84.38).

sections.h2: Property tax when you sell a Pierce County house
sections.html:
Each January 1, a lien for that year's property tax attaches to the parcel. If the contract is silent, RCW 84.60.020 makes you pay for the part of the year before closing and the buyer pay for the remainder. Escrow officers normally do the proration, taking any unpaid balance, interest or deferral out of your proceeds. Get a payoff figure before accepting an offer.

Sellers usually owe the state real estate excise tax too, payable to the county treasurer as of the sale date. The state share for sales on or after January 1, 2027 is 1.1% of the first $551,000, then 1.28% up to $1,551,000, 2.75% up to $3,051,000 and 3% beyond, and the local share is extra.

Moving does not have to cost you a senior exemption. A claimant who sells or is displaced can carry exemption status to a replacement residence under RCW 84.36.381, although only one home per year can hold it.

sections.h2: If you are behind on Pierce County property taxes
sections.html:
Foreclosure over unpaid tax takes years. RCW 84.64.050 bars a certificate of delinquency until three years after the delinquency date, and none can be filed when the unpaid tax is $100 or less. Owners and holders of recorded interests are notified and given thirty days to appear or pay.

You have choices before then. The treasurer can set up a payment agreement or take partial payments. As the three-year mark approaches, the treasurer must waive outstanding interest and penalties for an owner with limited income who lives in the home and never got a waiver before (RCW 84.56.020). Payments aimed at avoiding foreclosure go to the Assessor-Treasurer's Office, Attention: Foreclosure Avoidance, 2401 South 35th Street, Room 142, Tacoma, WA 98409-1498.

When back taxes make keeping the house impractical, request a payoff figure from the treasurer and let your escrow officer settle it from the sale proceeds. A cash buyer can shorten the timeline, since no lender review is involved.

faqs.q: When is the second half of Pierce County property tax due?
faqs.a: It is due October 31, or the following Monday when that date is a weekend, as it was in 2026. For a balance with interest on anything unpaid, call (253) 798-6111.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Pierce County assessment?
faqs.a: Dial (253) 798-6111 for the Assessor-Treasurer's Office. The Board of Equalization, which supplies appeal forms, is at (253) 798-7415.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal if July 1 has gone by?
faqs.a: Often. With a value change notice in hand, your deadline is whichever is later, July 1 or 60 days from the mailing date. Boards can also take a late petition for good cause.

faqs.q: Does the senior exemption follow me to a new home?
faqs.a: Yes, in many cases. Under RCW 84.36.381 a person who sells or is displaced may transfer exemption status to a replacement residence. One exempt home per year is the limit.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax at closing in Pierce County?
faqs.a: Whatever your contract says. Without a clause, the seller owes taxes through the day before the sale and the buyer owes the remainder. Escrow does the math.
